1–22 October 2026 · Burgers 2D/3D · JCP paper

Three weeks of Tunable NM-ROM

From Hari's off-mesh quadrature, through the JCP accuracy lanes and the Burgers campaign, to the improvement campaign that is finishing now. Every plot below comes straight from a lane's own output.

HoldsCost is set by the bank width, not the mesh. Accuracy does not depend on the mesh. Off-mesh quadrature and second-order steps made the model accurate.
Does not hold on the Burgers boxSpeed against a tuned spectral solver; speed against tuned POD + ECSW; a multi-mesh cost advantage; steeper fronts than training; complex geometry.
Still runningE1, the box family-width × steepness experiment (provisional plot at the end).

1–9 October

Hari's off-mesh quadrature and the accuracy lanes

The off-mesh classical quadrature was put inside our full-scale Burgers models, and four accuracy lanes tested what actually improves the reduced model.

13 October

Second-order references and the combined method

Second-order reference solutions (E0) replaced the old first-order ones, so accuracy numbers stopped being provisional. The combined method (second-order steps plus the wider bank) was scored against them.

17–20 October

Burgers 2D/3D campaign (ten lanes, 168.8 GPU-h)

The campaign answered the advisor's question (does cost depend on the bank width, not the mesh?) and compared the method against the strongest alternatives.

21–22 October

Improvement campaign: trying to fix the three weaknesses

Ten experiments, each with a stop rule written down before it ran. Accuracy is against the E0 references; speed-ups are upper bounds against the tested competitor ladders.
